key_insight: Training 3D anomaly detectors with only normal samples plus a few labeled anomalous examples (open-set supervised setting) enables reliable detection of previously unseen defects. The paper provides a high-quality industrial 3D dataset and a generalisable framework tuned for this practical scenario.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between purely self-supervised 3D anomaly detection and real manufacturing needs by enabling models to learn from limited anomalous examples while still identifying unknown defects at test time.
method: Collect and release Open-Industry: a curated industrial 3D point-cloud dataset containing normal parts, a small set of known defect types, and held-out unknown defects for evaluation.

Train a point-cloud anomaly detector in an open-set supervised regime: use normals + few known anomalies with specialized loss/augmentation to encourage separation of anomalous patterns while preserving generalisation to unseen defects.
Evaluate generalisability with protocols that measure detection of held-out (unknown) defect types and compare robustness across different defect scarcity settings.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical paradigm and dataset to build defect-detection systems that work in real factories where collecting a few defective samples is feasible—reducing reliance on costly anomaly simulation or exhaustive labeling while improving safety and quality control.
visual_elements: Side-by-side 3D point-cloud examples: normal vs known anomaly vs unknown anomaly (color-coded)
Pipeline diagram: dataset → open-set training (normals + few anomalies) → test-time unknown-defect detection

Bar chart comparing detection rates for known vs unknown defects across methods or data-scarcity regimes
paper_title: Open-Set Supervised 3D Anomaly Detection: An Industrial Dataset and a Generalisable Framework for Unknown Defects
paper_authors: Hanzhe Liang, Luocheng Zhang, Junyang Xia, HanLiang Zhou, Bingyang Guo
